newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle calls mixed, feeders steady to up.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle calls mixed, feeders steady to up.

text.p: Early calls on CME live cattle futures ranged from 0.100 cent per lb higher to 0.100 lower while feeder cattle were called steady to up 0.100 cent, livestock analysts said.
Some analysts expect rising wholesale beef prices and higher fed cattle markets to prompt early demand.

The price of choice heavy-weight boxed beef ran up another $1.20 per cwt to $108.58, the highest since December 4, 1995, and choice-type cattle sold at $69 per cwt Wednesday, the higest level since late February.

However, others look for cattle and beef markets to top soon. That expectation could weigh on futures. Retailer beef buying for Memorial Day should be complete by the end of the week. Packers were seen buying cattle actively for next week's operations but demand should ease when beef stocks reach a level that will satisfy booked sales through the late-month holiday, they said.
Some analysts also look for resistance to develop going into the next Cattle-on-Feed report. That report should indicate larger on-feed supplies, they said.

Feeder cattle futures were seen rising on an overall strong trend in cash feeder cattle markets. Although the latest CME feeder cattle index weakened and corn futures were called steady to higher, active feedlot cattle sales this week and last, and brisk corn plantings will likely keep interest for replacement feeders strong, they said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was off $0.14 to $73.20 per cwt.
